newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:
In answer to a question spokesman Thierry Daman said member states could not give themselves the right to opt out of Economic and Monetary Union.
Daman also said the items on Genetical modifed rapeseed and on the harmonisation of insurance credits had been postponed until June 18's Commission meeting.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/477: Free movement of capital and right of establishment: the case of intra-Community investments.
- IP/97/478: Commission adopts Single Market action plan for Amsterdam European Council.
- IP/97/479: Commission challenges vine planting scheme in France.
- IP/97/481: Promoting the development of Voluntary Organisations and Foundations in Europe.
- IP/97/482: Commission raises no objection to state aid scheme for Swedish shipping.
- IP/97/483: Information and consultation of employees at national level.
- IP/97/485: The Commission decides to close an investigation on research and development aid to Olivetti S.p.a.
- IP/97/487: State Aid: Germany - The Commission approves the creation of Berlin Land liquidity funds in favour of enterprises in difficulty.
- IP/97/488: The Commission clears the acquisition of 21% of Vallourec by Mannesmannroehren-Werke and the establishment of a joint venture combining their seamless tube activities.
- Speech/97/129: Speech by Commissioner Padraig Flynn on "For a Europe of civil and social rights".
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Economy and Finance No 1997-18: EU direct investment flows.
